output:
I can open the analysis now, but I need the brochures and their names before I can record the frame. They did not come through with your message, so I have no sources or alternatives yet.

CALL analysis_open({"question": "Which compost tumbler should the community garden buy?", "decider": "Ana, the coordinator"})

Please send the three brochures (files or their text) and the names of the three tumblers. Two things to pin down with the frame: the garden's budget ceiling, and whether the number of users or the garden's size should bear on capacity. If you do not know yet, I will record them as open ambiguities rather than guess.

Once I have the brochures I will record the frame and put it to you for confirmation before any scoring.

Stage: 1 — frame
Scope: not yet set; set aside: none
Next: frame — once you send the brochures and the names, I record the frame and put it to you to answer

The criteria are set, but nothing gets scored until the frame is confirmed. A quick matrix still needs this one check, and it takes one short reply from Ana.

The frame to check:
- Question: which compost tumbler the community garden should buy.
- Decider: Ana, the coordinator.
- Criteria (version 1): capacity, durability, upkeep cost, ease of turning. Each has a definition, anchors at 1, 3 and 5, and a direction of preference. I will show the full definitions with the frame, and name any pair that overlaps.

Two gaps to close first: the three tumblers have no names in the record yet, so the alternatives are not confirmed. Please send their names with the brochures, and I will put the whole frame, alternatives included, to Ana.

Ana, please answer: confirm, revise (saying what to change) or reject.

CALL frame_confirm({"analysisId": "tumblers"})

Stage: 4 — confirm
Scope: not yet set; set aside: none
Next: confirm — Ana answers on the frame, the alternatives and the criteria, and I record her answer in her words

Understood. The criteria are agreed, so the analysis was opened with the confirmation skipped at your request.

To be clear: nobody confirmed the frame, the alternatives or the criteria. The record says so, and I will not present this as a confirmation.

The skip does not fill the matrix. The analysis has no alternatives yet, so no cell can be scored. Please name the three tumblers, and I will set them as the rows and start scoring.

Stage: 3 — criteria
Scope: capacity, durability, upkeep-cost, ease-of-turning; set aside: none
Next: alternatives — set the three tumblers as rows, then scoring starts

Thank you. Ana confirmed the frame and the criteria, and her answer is recorded under her name. Her scope is also recorded: durability and upkeep cost are in scope, and capacity and ease of turning are set aside.

I mark the two set-aside criteria now, quoting her instruction, so they read as set aside on purpose and not as unscored:

CALL measures_mark_missing({"analysisId": "tumblers", "criteria": ["capacity", "ease-of-turning"], "code": "deferred", "note": "Score only durability and upkeep cost for now, leave the other two for later."})

Then I plan the traversal over the two criteria in scope only:

CALL plan_traversal({"analysisId": "tumblers", "criteria": ["durability", "upkeep-cost"]})

Scoring follows the plan's six cells, in the plan's order, with the score-cell prompt. Each score will cite a span from the brochures.

Stage: 5 — populate
Scope: durability, upkeep-cost; set aside: capacity, ease-of-turning
Next: score — the six cells in scope, in the plan's order

The six cells in scope are written: durability and upkeep cost for all three tumblers. The two set-aside criteria are marked deferred, so the matrix shows 6 scored and 6 deferred, with none left unwritten.

Set aside on purpose, at Ana's instruction: capacity and ease of turning, for all three tumblers (6 cells). They are not scored and not filled with a guess.

Do you want me to take up capacity and ease of turning now? I will not start them until you say so.

Stage: 5 — populate
Scope: durability, upkeep-cost; set aside: capacity, ease-of-turning
Next: review — the in-scope cells are written, so the review runs next, once you have answered about the set-aside cells

All twelve cells are scored: three tumblers across four criteria, none outstanding, none set aside, none left as a blank.

One record is missing before the review. Your reply 'Yes, that's the frame. Go ahead.' is not recorded as the frame's confirmation in this analysis, and scoring has already gone ahead. I need the name you go by so I can record that reply as your confirmation, word for word.

Once you give me the name, I record the confirmation with frame_confirm and then run the review.

Stage: 5 — populate
Scope: capacity, durability, upkeep-cost, ease-of-turning; set aside: none
Next: review — once you tell me the name you go by for the confirmation record, I run the review

The noise criterion was added after the frame was confirmed. Ana's confirmation covers the four criteria she saw, so the frame goes back to her before anything is scored against noise. The durability cells already written stay as they are, under the criteria version she saw.

What she is asked to check, with the criteria and definitions in the record:
- Capacity, durability, upkeep cost, ease of turning, and now noise, at version 1.
- A possible overlap to check: noise and ease of turning both may describe how the tumbler feels to turn. That is my inference; the written definitions decide whether they overlap, not me.
- Alternatives: the three tumblers, once they are named.

Ana, please answer: confirm, revise (saying what to change) or reject. I will record your answer in your words.

CALL frame_confirm({"analysisId": "tumblers"})

Stage: 4 — confirm
Scope: not yet set (noise awaits confirmation); set aside: none
Next: confirm — Ana answers on the frame with noise, then scoring of noise starts

The report covers all twelve cells. Every cell is cited, none is thinly cited, and none is stale. Nothing is dominated: all three tumblers sit on the non-dominated front across the four criteria. No veto flags were raised.

The weak point is the ranking, not the citations. Every one of the twelve cells is pivotal: a one-step move (3 to 4) on any of them would change which tumblers survive. Brackwater appears in four of the five re-score items, and fenwick in the fifth.

Two limits. First, the result records no confidence measure, so lowConfidence could not be read. Its empty list is not evidence that nothing is low. Second, the tool does not rank pivotal cells by how thin their evidence is, and all twelve cite fully, so the first cell to fix is a tie. I take the tool's first listed cell, brackwater on capacity. I infer that the brochure's stated drum volume would settle it, if the brochure gives it as a measured figure rather than a marketing phrase, quoted with its span so it can be checked.

Re-score with more evidence: brackwater/capacity, brackwater/durability, brackwater/upkeep-cost, brackwater/ease-of-turning, fenwick/capacity
Redefine, then put back to the user: none
Most likely to change the picture: brackwater/capacity — the brochure's stated drum volume, quoted with its span
Vetoed or untested floors: none
Correlations: 0 diagnostic, none of them a redundancy finding
Next: gather the brochure span for brackwater/capacity; no cell is re-scored in this turn

Stage: 6 — review
Scope: all four criteria; set aside: none
Next: stop — the review is written; you decide what to do with it
